newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares cling to small gains in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares cling to small gains in light trade.

text.p: Pre-Easter sentiment hit Norwegian shares on Monday and Oslo's Total index drifted off from the day's highs but managed to hold in positive territory in lackluster trade.

The bourse will close at 1200 GMT on Wednesday for the Easter holidays and dealers said activity was likely to remain muted. The index closed 0.08 percent up at 1,064.98 points in dull turnover of 468 million crowns.
"Most people have taken the week off," said one broker. "Any change in interest rates in the United States has already been discounted for, we don't expect to see much happen."

The banks remained centre of attention following the outbreak of a bidding war betweeen Fokus Bank and Den norske Bank (DnB) for mortgage lender BNbank last week. Fokus Bank was the most traded share in value terms, accounting for 42.8 million crowns of turnover. The stock lost 0.50 crowns to end at 58.50 crowns.

DnB, which said it is unlikely to respond to a revised offer by Fokus until after Easter was third in the turnover list at 27.2 million crowns, with Norsk Hydro creeping in at second place at 33.7 million crowns. DnB closed 0.10 down at 27.90 crowns, while Hydro lost two crowns to end at 333 crowns.
